Subject: Post-demo token economics debrief + next tests

Hi Jason — great demo earlier, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan for the POC: 

Recap (what we covered)
- Competitive delta: we reviewed Redwood vs HyperscaleX (their managed inference) and BigCloud’s serverless endpoints. Key customer asks: predictable unit cost, consistent P95 latency, and cache-aware billing.
- Redwood differentiators called out on the call: predictable dedicated pools, prefix/KV caching that reduces effective token usage, workload-aware batching, and quantization profiles that preserve quality while lowering GPU cost.

Initial unit economics (ballpark, for planning tests)
- Redwood hosted (standard config): list price ~ $9.00 per 1M tokens; effective cost with realistic prefix cache hits (50%) could be ~$3.75 per 1M tokens.
- HyperscaleX managed endpoint: list price shown during call ~ $18.00 per 1M tokens, no built-in prefix cache (customer-level cache needed).
- BigCloud serverless: variable — cheaper at very low QPS but cost climbs with sustained throughput when autoscale kicks in; rough crossover at ~400 qps for sustained workloads.

Proposed POC tests (what Acme asked for)
1) Per-1M token baseline: run 1M token generation with: no cache, 50% prefix cache, 80% prefix cache. Measure raw token count, effective billed tokens, and overall cost.
2) Batching: compare client-side micro-batching (N=4,8) vs Redwood server-side continuous batching; measure P50/P95 latency and tokens/sec.
3) KV cache sensitivity: run synthetic replay with cache-hit scenarios at 20/50/80% and log cache hit ratio + effect on GPU utilization.
4) Model variants: compare fp16 baseline vs int8 quantized variant for cost and top-line accuracy degradation (we'll keep a small eval set).
5) Routing & fallback: simulate a brief capacity bump and observe Redwood’s policy-based fallback (variant routing) — measure any latency spikes and spillover cost.

Deliverables we’ll provide
- Measurement matrix & test harness (spreadsheet attached)
- KV cache test script (we’ll share as executable + instructions)
- Telemetry format for token-level cost (so your infra team can ingest)

Timeline & next steps
- Proposed kickoff week: Mon Jun 7 — Wed Jun 9 (half-day kickoff + test-run day + results recap).
- Action owners: Redwood to supply scripts + spreadsheet by Fri May 28 (Naomi), Acme to whitelist test IPs and share a small eval prompt set by Tue Jun 1 (Jason).
- Goal: produce per-scenario effective cost (per-1M adjusted tokens), P95 latency, and a go/no-go recommendation for dedicated capacity.

Attachments: per-1M token cost model (spreadsheet) and initial KV-cache script stub.

If that looks right I’ll lock the kickoff time and send calendar invites.

Best,

Thanks Naomi — solid plan. Two technical clarifications to add to the test matrix: 

1) Quantized model variants: when we compare fp16 vs int8, we should capture token-level output divergence on the Acme eval prompts (we should include a tiny automated eval harness that computes BLEU/ROUGE or semantic-similarity scores). Int8 will typically cut GPU/memory cost ~30-40% depending on kernel path, so that needs to be in the spreadsheet.

2) Dedicated capacity crossover: add a simple cost model row that shows the break-even point (tokens/day and sustained QPS) where committed dedicated pools become cheaper than per-token hosted. For many customers the crossover is at sustained usage > ~250k generated tokens/day with predictable latency needs.

Proposed measurement matrix additions (short)
- Add columns: eval-quality-delta, GPU-hours consumed, model-variant, routing-policy (dedicated vs hosted).
- For cache hit tests, capture both prefix hits and KV-cache hits separately — some workloads benefit more from one than the other.

Also — we'll need to confirm which HyperscaleX SKU Jason was referencing. Jason, can you forward the pricing link or screenshot from your team? That will help keep apples-to-apples.

Quick additions from CS/implementation side: 

- Client-side vs server-side batching: make sure we run both the micro-batching driver (simulate many parallel small requests aggregated client-side) and Redwood continuous batching. Common gotcha: client batching reduces RPC overhead but can hurt tail latency if the client waits to fill a batch. We'll capture request queuing time vs GPU time.

- Tracing & telemetry: we need a small wrapper that emits token-level trace ids so we can reconcile costs back to user sessions. I’ll draft the wrapper and include a README in the shared Drive.

- Dependencies: we may need a short firewall/egress allowlist for the dedicated pool. Jason — if you have an infra contact, please share their email so we can coordinate.

I attached a short doc (client-batching-vs-server-batching.md) with test scenarios and expected observability fields.
